discovery: Discovery of current-induced spin-orbit torques and their use for electrical switching of magnetization
motivation: Miron and Gambardella showed in 2010-2011 that an in-plane current in heavy-metal/ferromagnet bilayers (Pt/Co/AlOx) exerts spin-orbit torques large enough to switch a perpendicular magnet deterministically. Buhrman's group identified the spin Hall effect in Ta, Pt and W as an efficient source of pure spin currents, and in 2012 demonstrated three-terminal spin-Hall switching and spin-torque oscillation. These discoveries turned relativistic spin-orbit coupling into a practical way to control magnetism electrically. The read and write paths are separated, so write currents no longer pass through the tunnel barrier. This solves the endurance and speed problems of spin-transfer-torque MRAM and has made SOT-MRAM a leading candidate for fast embedded cache memory. The same torques drive chiral domain walls and skyrmions and power spin Hall nano-oscillators and neuromorphic arrays. This is a new physical mechanism, proven by clean experiments and now moving into technology.
